newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Payrolls give U.S. edge over Europe.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Payrolls give U.S. edge over Europe.

text.p: Global bond markets powered higher on Thursday as they breathed a sigh of relief at the fairly modest rise in U.S. jobs growth in June.
Analysts said the 217,000 rise in non-farm payrolls had slightly dampened expectations of a U.S. rate rise in August and would help the longer end of the Treasury curve to outperform Europe.
"I think at the longer end, there's clearly an argument for Treasury market outperformance," Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi told Reuters Financial Television.
"Until we get a report to upset the rosy scenario, Treasuries will continue to outperform Europe," Chester added.

The T-bond/Bund spread snapped in seven basis points to 80 basis points after the labour report. By 1304 GMT September T-bond futures were up 1-2/32 at 113-04 while September Bunds on LIFFE were up 31 basis points at 102.33, off a new contract high set earlier at 102.35.

The data showed average earnings per hour edged up to $12.22 in June from $12.18 in May and the unemployment rate nudged up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent in May. Non-farm payrolls were revised up to 166,000 in May from a previously reported 138,000.
BZW analyst Phyllis Reed also expected the Treasury market to get a boost over core Europe.

"I very much think that spread will narrow further," she said. "In particular, core Europe looks very expensive relative to the U.S. given all the problems with EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union)."
"I don't think the risk premium that comes along with a softer EMU scenario is priced into the market at the moment," Reed added.
She expected the T-bond/Bund spread to narrow to 50 basis points by the end of the year and did not rule out the spread closing up altogether next year.
Reed noted the relative supply profiles in Germany and the U.S. also favoured a narrowing of the spread with the U.S. cutting its supply targets and Germany having to increase its.
But Graham McDevitt, head of bond strategy at Paribas Capital Markets in London, was much more pessimistic about the performance of Treasuries against core Europe.
"Looking ahead to a one, two or three month view, I'd have to be short Treasuries versus core Europe, looking for that spread with Bunds to go back out to 100 basis points," he said.
McDevitt said the rally in Treasuries had largely run its course with a lot of good news already priced into the curve.
"So I wouldn't be looking to buy that (T-bond/Bund) spread, I'd be looking to sell it," he said.
McDevitt said the relief rally in Treasuries had helped fuel already well-bid European markets.
He said the short squeeze in Bunds was coming to end, limiting the upside in the German market, but noted that EMU hopefuls Italy, Spain and Portugal had further to rise.
He expected the BTP/Bund spread to contract to 90 basis points near term from 104 currently. "There's real momentum in these markets," he said.
